blogs.title: The Pre-Op Cath Trap: Why Early Post-Cardiac Surgery Thrombocytopenia Isn't Always 'Normal'
blogs.description: This post challenges the dogma that HIT cannot occur before post-operative day 5 in cardiac surgery patients. Using this case, we explore how pre-operative heparin exposure during diagnostic catheterization can prime the immune system, leading to 'accelerated' autoimmune HIT (aHIT) immediately after bypass. We will discuss the critical importance of taking a detailed anticoagulation history beyond the operating room to avoid missing early-onset, life-threatening thrombosis.

blogs.title: When the Gold Standard Fails: Decoding Atypical Serotonin Release Assays in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: A deep dive into the laboratory diagnostics of aHIT, focusing on cases where the confirmatory Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) yields 'indeterminate' or confusing results. We analyze the specific finding of heparin-independent platelet activation and, crucially, the novel observation of partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade. This post teaches clinicians and laboratorians how to recognize severe aHIT even when classical inhibitory patterns are absent, preventing false negatives in high-stakes scenarios.

blogs.title: Beyond Thrombocytopenia: Recognizing Consumptive Coagulopathy and Schistocytes in Severe aHIT
blogs.description: Classic teaching suggests HIT presents with isolated thrombocytopenia and thrombosis, sparing the coagulation cascade. This case illustrates a dangerous exception: severe aHIT mimicking DIC or TTP with falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimers, and schistocytosis. We discuss the pathophysiology of this intense hypercoagulable state, why it often resists standard Direct Thrombin Inhibitors like argatroban, and when to suspect aHIT in patients presenting with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia features post-surgery.

blogs.title: Escalating Therapy: The Role of IVIG and Fondaparinux When Argatroban Isn't Enough
blogs.description: Management strategies for refractory autoimmune HIT. This post analyzes the clinical decision-making process when a patient continues to deteriorate on argatroban despite high-dose IVIG. We evaluate the rationale for switching to therapeutic-dose fondaparinux (an off-label but potent option), the necessity of antithrombin supplementation for efficacy, and compare the pros and cons of various non-heparin anticoagulants in the setting of recent neurosurgical events and severe thrombocytopenia.
